text:
Alex: heads-up — saw a short ECC/Xid spike on gpunode-43 this morning and the auto-cordon drained it. pods restarted and a couple of jobs lost progress :confused:
Jordan: can you paste the driver logs and the alert that triggered the cordon?
Alex: logs attached in the incident email but snippet here:
```
[2026-03-18T07:12:01Z] GPU0 Xid: 79 count=12
[2026-03-18T07:12:12Z] GPU0 Xid: 79 count=15
[2026-03-18T07:15:02Z] GPU0 recovered, no further Xid
```
Mira: looks like a bursty pattern rather than sustained failure. the current rule is a single-threshold which is too sensitive.
Sam: agreed. we should avoid full node drains for <5m transient spikes, especially for latency-critical pods.
Priya: proposal: implement a "fuzzyband" detector — two thresholds + cooldown. transient_threshold => mark node degraded and start re-eval timer. sustained_threshold => cordon+drain. add exponential backoff for repeated drains.
Mira: algorithm sketch:
- keep EWMA of Xid_rate per GPU
- if EWMA > transient_threshold for T_window (1m) => annotate node as "gpu-degraded"
- wait for re-eval interval (5m). if EWMA falls below transient_threshold -> clear annotation
- if EWMA > sustained_threshold for sustained_window (3m) => auto-cordon + drain
- circuit-breaker: suppress auto-drain for nodes with recent successful recovery count > N
Jordan: will need telemetry: per-gpu metrics: gpu_xid_count, gpu_ecc_count, gpu_recovery_count. add labels: node, gpu_id, driver_version. I can add prometheus exporters.
Sam: k8s integration notes:
- annotate nodes instead of immediate cordon so ops can inspect:
  kubectl annotate node gpunode-43 redwood/gpu-status=degraded
- cordon+drain only on sustained rule:
  kubectl cordon gpunode-43 && kubectl drain gpunode-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- for pods with label "redwood/no-evict=true" skip drain and escalate to human
Priya: Slurm path: map the same detector to scontrol actions. transient => set node state=RESUME (no-op), sustained => scontrol update NodeName=gpunode-43 State=DOWN Reason=GPU_SUSTAINED_XID. Use scontrol requeue for jobs if appropriate.
Mira: config snippet for the feature flag (ConfigMap) - example:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gpu-fuzzyband-config
data:
  transient_threshold: "10"  # xid/min per GPU
  transient_window_s: "60"
  reeval_s: "300"
  sustained_threshold: "30"
  sustained_window_s: "180"
  suppress_backoff_minutes: "60"
```
Alex: testing plan: simulate Xid bursts with probe that pumps synthetic error events into node exporter, run canary on dedicated-gpu-pool-beta (10% nodes). monitor job retry rate and node churn.
Sam: cost tradeoffs: under-drain => failed jobs and wasted GPU hours; over-drain => scheduling churn and capacity fragmentation. need dashboards to show wasted GPU-hours / avoided failures.
Jordan: I'll add metrics to prometheus: rate(gpu_xid_count[1m]), increase(gpu_recovery_count[5m]). we'll create alert: gpu_fuzzyband_sustained{pool="beta"} firing only when sustained rule true.
Mira: dashboard panels: per-pool Xid rate heatmap, per-node EWMA sparkline, recent cordon events table.
Priya: rollout timeline: prototype (2d), integration & tests (3d), canary to beta pool (1w), expand if stable.
Alex: owners: Mira (detector algo + dashboards), Jordan (telemetry + alerts), Sam (k8s drain integration), Priya (slurm mapping + ops runbook). I'll open RFC PR with config + tests.
ops-bot: created ticket INC-4231 and ran preflight checks for gpunode-43; no other nodes in pool exceed transient threshold.
Sam: +1. we should also add a human-in-loop escalation channel if auto-drain suppressed but repeated degradations occur.
Alex: yep — add Slack notify to #eng-oncall with ephemeral action buttons (ack/dismiss/force-drain).
Mira: one more: add minor ML model to classify multi-metric failure signatures (xid+ecc+temperature spikes) vs noisy drivers. can be low-cost rule-based first.
Jordan: ok i'll instrument and send a PR for exporter and alert rules by EOD.
Alex: thanks all — great outcome. will track RFC and test results. :thumbsup:
